text: Large language models, or LLMs, are computer programs trained on massive amounts of text from books, websites, and articles. They work by predicting the next word in a sequence, using patterns they learned from this training data. When you give an LLM a prompt, it uses those patterns to generate a response that sounds natural. Prompt engineering is the skill of writing clear, specific instructions to get the best possible output—for example, asking for a summary instead of just "help me." These models are impressive at writing, translating, and answering questions, but they have limits. They can make mistakes, repeat false information, and lack real-world understanding, so you should always check their answers.
